complexity.notes: Each word's key is computed twice (once when building the dict, once when appending); using defaultdict(list) in a single loop would avoid the redundant work and the double pass. The return annotation tuple(int) is invalid type-hint syntax (should be tuple[int, ...]), and ord(letter)-97 is less readable than ord(letter)-ord('a'). [d[group] for group in d] could be written as list(d.values()).
complexity.summary: Maps each word to a 26-element character-count tuple and uses that tuple as a dict key to bucket anagrams together. With word lengths bounded (3-8 chars), building each key is O(1), so grouping is linear in the number of words.
